At different table positions git applies both additions cleanly and the duplicate id is silent.

THE_GAP.claim: A duplicate-id check exists, is correct, runs against the real file, and covers ONE of the four id-bearing ledgers -- the one where the LAST incident happened.
THE_GAP.where_the_check_lives: docs/orchestration/whose_row.py:436 check_ledger_ids(), reached from :551 as `check_ledger_ids(REPO / 'VALIDATION_LEDGER.md')`, and invoked by docs/orchestration/merge_guard.sh via `--check-ledger-ids`.
THE_GAP.what_it_catches: half-finished re-id, rows deleted after id assignment, DUPLICATED ids, renumbered-from-N, gaps. Two-sided, and the two directions fail with opposite signs.
THE_GAP.why_it_did_not_fire_on_OI-48: It is only ever called with VALIDATION_LEDGER.md. Its id parsing is VL-specific too, not merely its call site: `nums = [int(v[2:]) for v in ids]` strips two characters, which yields -48 for `OI-48` and raises for `BEN-118`.
THE_GAP.the_patterns_already_exist_beside_it: whose_row.py:65 BEN_ROW, :66 CLM_ROW, :74 VL_ROW, :75 OI_ROW. All four id shapes are already parsed in this file for attribution. Only VL is passed to the uniqueness check.
THE_GAP.class: The same shape D and C filed tonight -- a remedy bounded to the exact object that failed. `lane_matches` rebuilt and `conflicted_line_numbers` not (BEN-162); predicate tested and call path not (BEN-117); code fixed and published contract not (BEN-163); and now uniqueness enforced on the ledger that had the re-id incident, not on the ledger class. The VL re-id was the occasion for writing it, and the occasion set the scope.

MEASURED_NOW -- no duplicates exist yet,.A_FIFTH_INSTANCE_LANDED_WHILE_THIS_WAS_B: Session A reports allocating OI-49..OI-52 against its own checkout while C had already landed OI-49 and OI-50. So the count is now FOUR writers colliding on the OI namespace within about two hours, on two different ids. That one was caught by `merge_guard.sh A`, which refused and named C -- the gate working, on the conflict path rather than the uniqueness path. It does not close this finding: the gate caught a CONFLICTED row, which requires the rows to overlap textually. The silent case is two same-id rows at different table positions, which never conflict. A's own conclusion is that `OI-*` wants block partitioning like `BEN-*`, and A notes correctly that a convention change is not one lane's to make.
MEASURED_NOW -- no duplicates exist yet,.KNOWN_BLIND_SPOT_REPORTED_NOT_HIDDEN: KNOWN_ISSUES.md matched ZERO rows for `KI-\d+` and is therefore UNSCANNED, not clean. Its items are numbered in prose ('item 26'), not id-prefixed, so it has no per-row id scheme to check -- the same property that makes VALIDATION_LEDGER.md's rows unattributable before the VL re-id. Reported as a cannot-check rather than counted as a pass.

THE_DESIGN_CONSTRAINT -- DO NOT JUST WID.warning: check_ledger_ids bundles THREE invariants and only one of them generalises. Calling it unchanged on FINDINGS.md would fail on 64 gaps and on min(nums)=1 density.
THE_DESIGN_CONSTRAINT -- DO NOT JUST WID.universal: NO DUPLICATE IDS. True of every id-bearing ledger, and the only one the OI-48 incident needed.
THE_DESIGN_CONSTRAINT -- DO NOT JUST WID.VL_only: dense from 1, no gaps. Correct for VALIDATION_LEDGER.md because its ids were assigned in one pass over every row; WRONG for FINDINGS.md, whose 64 gaps are legitimate -- rows moved to FINDINGS-ARCHIVE-2026-08.md -- and wrong for any ledger with per-lane blocks, where gaps are the blocks.
THE_DESIGN_CONSTRAINT -- DO NOT JUST WID.why_this_matters_more_than_it_looks: A widened check would fire 64 false failures on the first run, through merge_guard.sh, which exits 3 and BLOCKS THE MERGE. That is BEN-118's own second half: a check that refuses for the wrong reason teaches operators to override it, and an override habit is how the next true failure gets waved through. The gate is load-bearing on every lane's merge, so a false-positive there is more expensive than the hole it closes.
